chunks: By this chain, from Fazalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Qunut in the obligatory prayer is supplication, and in the Witr is the seeking of forgiveness.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Qunut in obligatory prayer and Qunut in Witr?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes the spiritual intent behind the Qunut in daily obligatory prayers versus the Witr prayer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on specific devotional nuances. It highlights the transition from general supplication for worldly and spiritual needs in Fard prayers to the focused purification of sins through Istighfar in the concluding Witr prayer, a practice deeply rooted in the Ahl al-Bayt's tradition.

en.hubeali:
By this chain, from Fazalat, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Qunut in the Obligatory (Salāt) is the supplication, and in the Witr (Salāt), it is the seeking of Forgiveness’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Aban from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah, who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
‘Al-Qunut in obligatory Salah (prayer) is pleading (before Allah) and in Witr it is to ask forgiveness (from Allah).’” (Ahadith 1-9 are best explained in the form of fatwa.)
